subject: Linguistics
title: Standard and Nonstandard Varieties
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Standard and Nonstandard Varieties.

hook.text: 'He don't know nothing' is nonstandard English—but it follows a perfectly logical double-negative rule.

buildup.text: Standard varieties are those promoted in education, media, and government.

discovery.text: Nonstandard varieties are equally rule-governed—they just follow different rules.

twist.text: The standard is usually the dialect of the most powerful social group—not the 'best' one.

climax.text: Linguists distinguish between correctness (social norm) and grammaticality (systematic pattern).

punchline.text: Every dialect has grammar—some just have more prestige.

quiz.question: Why is a language variety considered 'standard'?
